Thanks for the demo today — the team found the latency consistency on the Dedicated run compelling. A couple quick clarifications from our side so we can move this toward sizing/procurement:

- Deployment preference: leaning toward Dedicated capacity (predictable latency, isolation). We still want to understand the tradeoffs vs Hosted API if burst spots are needed.
- Targets: peak ~12 TPS for the inference endpoint during US business hours, sustained ~4 TPS outside peak.
- Latency SLO: aiming for ~350ms P95 for most requests; sub-200ms would be nice for our short prompts but not mandatory.
- Token mix: approx 70% short prompts (20–60 tokens), 30% long contexts (1k–2k tokens) for multi-turn summarization.
- Model family: currently evaluating Llama-2-Chat and Mistral-7B; open to quantized variants if quality holds.

I've attached a quick token_profile export (samira_token_profile.csv) and a rough internal SOW template they'll likely use for procurement. Can you (1) propose a dedicated sizing scenario (GPU type recommendation + expected concurrency), and (2) call out where Hosted would materially differ (cost/latency/fallback)?

Thanks — Lina

Karthik / Ben — below are the high-level constraints Lina sent and my initial hypotheses. Please review and add any benchmarking artifacts youll want priors for.

Customer constraints:
- Peak 12 TPS (US business window) / sustained ~4 TPS
- Token mix skewed to short requests (70%) with 30% long contexts (1k–2k)
- P95 target ~350ms (long-context may be relaxed)

Hypotheses and immediate questions:
1) GPU family: H100 will give better single-request latency at high concurrency for autoregressive decoders, but A100 may be more cost-effective given their long-context fraction is only 30%. Recommend we model both H100-80GB and A100-40GB scenarios.
2) KV cache: long-context flows will benefit from larger KV-memory and reduced cache thrashing. Need to know average long-context active sequence length and typical multi-turn session length.
3) Batching: with 12 TPS and 70% short, we can use ~dynamic batching with target batch sizes 4–16 for token efficiency; need to quantify P95 impact.
4) Quantization: 4-bit (GPTQ) may be viable for Mistral-7B; Llama-2-family may need 8-bit to preserve quality. We should call out QA steps for quality regression.

Data asks for profiling run (from customer):
- 200 anonymized request samples (header + token counts) with timestamps
- Any existing p95/p99 latency measurements from their dev runs

Ill take the A100 scenario and run token-level cost + latency estimates; Ben, can you model the H100 throughput/costs?

Thanks — Priyom

Nice summary — a few concrete questions and a suggested sizing scaffold below. Im attaching a quick GPU comparison table for reference.

Questions for Lina (we can paste these in the next outbound):
- Is the 12 TPS a sustained peak for >30m or a burst event (1–5 min)? This drives whether we need reserve headroom vs burstable cushion.
- For the 30% long-context: are those single requests of 1k–2k tokens, or multi-request concatenated sessions where effective context can grow >2k?
- Any hard SLA clauses in procurement (credits for >2h outage, P99 obligations)?

Sizing scaffold (back-of-envelope):
- A100-40GB scenario (cost-conscious): target 8–12 concurrent streams, expected P95 ~300–500ms (depends on batching). Good for workloads with higher token variance.
- H100-80GB scenario (latency-first): can sustain more simultaneous streams with lower tail latency — useful if they want <250ms P95 for short prompts at 12 TPS.
- Hybrid pool option: 70% A100 + 30% H100 to optimize cost vs latency for mixed token mixes.

Ill build the throughput matrix assuming: avg short request 40 tokens, avg long request 1500 tokens, generation ratio 0.6 (decode-heavy). Well need to validate with their actual samples.
